content.comment_body: I use [product_name] [article_no] and suspect there was a power issue (I wasn't present at the time). After this, the device wouldn't start and displayed an 'Empty program' error. Once I retransferred the program, everything worked again. As far as I know, no one deleted the program, so I'm unsure why this happened.

The program is stored in FLASH memory in the [product_name], so typically, it can't be lost. It's an unusual error. At my property using [product_name] [article_no], there have been several voltage interruptions, but the device always restarted and recovered without any issues. Which firmware does your device have? Mine runs on [version_no].
My [product_name] is new and uses [version_no]. I rebooted it without any problems—the program remains intact.

I asked about the firmware version because there's another discussion in the German forum regarding [product_name] devices with [version_no] that sporadically stop on their own, particularly when connected to other modules or operator panels.

analysis.insight_summary: Users noticed an unexpected loss of the user program on a [product_name] [article_no] after a power interruption, leading to an 'Empty program' message. However, others confirm that the program stored in FLASH memory should normally persist through power cycles. The issue seems connected to [version_no], which reportedly can cause the device to stop randomly, especially when linked with other devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that the [product_name] will reliably retain user programs during power failures and restart automatically, without requiring extra steps or causing any data loss.
